transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Time: 10:00 AM - 10:45 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Miguel Santos (Bluecrest Head of Data), Aisha Khan (Bluecrest ML Engineer), Leo Park (Bluecrest Product Owner)

Summary:
Quick sync on weekly POC quality results; went over prompt set updates, scoring regressions seen after yesterday's deploy, guardrail tuning for hallucination cases, and next steps to re-run the regression harness. Agreement to tighten pass threshold from 0.78 to 0.82 for the clinical-summary prompt family and to fix a tokenization preprocessing bug which likely caused false negatives.

Topics:
- Overall quality delta from last week
- Regression cases and root cause hypothesis (tokenization + prompt drift)
- Scoring rubric and thresholds (auto + human override)
- Guardrails and hallucination detection (system messages, QA heuristic)
- Next steps: run regression, share docs, potential Dedicated run if cost/latency tradeoffs change

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: All right good morning everyone, uh this is our weekly POC sync for Bluecrest, Jordan from Redwood here with Priya. Priya: hey hi.
[00:12] Dr. Miguel Santos: morning, thanks; we have Aisha and Leo on as well.
[00:20] Leo Park: morning hey.
[00:25] Jordan Lee: quick agenda - results, regressions we saw after the small prompt change yesterday, guardrail tuning, and action items. Take it away Priya with the results?
[00:33] Priya Patel: sure; so I pulled the automated eval we ran overnight - 1,000 prompts across the clinical-summary and triage categories. Overall pass-rate dropped by about 4.6% vs last week's baseline, so sorta noticeable. The clinical-summary family took the biggest hit - where previously we were at ~82% pass, now it's ~77.4%.
[01:05] Aisha Khan: yeah we noticed that on our side too; a bunch of cases where the model split sentences differently, likely from tokenization differences when we preprocessed the EHR notes. Some outputs were semantically ok but scored low because exact-match and token-overlap metrics failed.
[01:28] Priya Patel: exactly; we flag both automated metrics and a small human review sample. The human reviewers called out that many of the apparent failures were formatting / tokenization issues, not hallucination.
[01:40] Dr. Miguel Santos: can you remind me which metrics the harness is using? Is it BLEU/ROUGE/F1?
[01:45] Priya Patel: it's a combination - ROUGE-L for summary overlap, an F1 on key-entity extraction, and a hallucination heuristic which uses an NER mismatch plus a confidence threshold on the model's logits. We also have a human_gt column when we sample 100 items.
[02:03] Jordan Lee: and the scoring threshold we've been treating as pass is 0.78 overall - the weighted aggregator. After looking at the human samples we recommend pulling that up to 0.82 for clinical-summary to reduce false positives.
[02:18] Leo Park: ok - we just worry that raising thresholds might over-penalize good outputs. How would that affect our reported SLA?
[02:25] Jordan Lee: good question. We'll separate internal QA and SLA metrics; your external SLA isn't changing - this is for the POC acceptance criteria and to catch regressions earlier. If you want we can keep a dual-metric: strict for internal gating, soft for product-facing.
[02:41] Aisha Khan: the big blocker for us is the tokenization. I dug in and the whitespace normalization in our ETL removed some punctuation and collapsed hyphenated terms; that broke the entity matching so F1 took a hit.
[03:00] Priya Patel: thanks, that explains it. For the regression suite, we'll add a preprocessing check so the same pipeline runs locally and in the harness. Can you upload a small sample of the raw notes?
[03:12] Aisha Khan: yes I'll upload 2k sample records to the shared S3 link by EOD.
[03:18] Jordan Lee: perfect. On the hallucination front - we saw two categories: outright invented clinical conditions, and confident assertions without cite. We recommend adding a stricter system prompt that instructs the model to respond only when there's evidence in the note and otherwise say "insufficient information".
[03:40] Dr. Miguel Santos: will that increase abstention too much? We can't have the model say insufficient info on everything, our clinicians want something actionable.
[03:48] Priya Patel: it's a balance. We tested versions with 3 few-shot examples that show when to abstain; abstention rose from 2% to 6% but hallucinations dropped by ~80% in our small eval. You can tune few-shot selection to match your tolerance.
[04:05] Jordan Lee: also worth noting Redwood's guardrail layer supports a post-filter that triggers human-in-the-loop for high-risk classes, so if you mark some entities as high-risk e.g., diagnoses, we can escalate those.
[04:20] Leo Park: that sounds good. How invasive is that for latency?
[04:24] Priya Patel: the HIL path adds about 300-500ms for the routing check; actual review time depends on your ops. We can route to a review queue and show diffs in the console.
[04:36] Aisha Khan: back to regression - did you track which prompt variants caused the biggest drop? I remember we tried adding a clarification line yesterday.
[04:44] Priya Patel: yes, variant B (added clarifying system message and changed temperature from 0.2 to 0.15) is where we saw most of the delta. The lower temperature reduced diversity which improved factuality generally, but in combination with the tokenization mismatch it penalized reformatted phrases.
[05:03] Jordan Lee: so two things to do: 1) fix preprocessing to avoid token mismatch; 2) we recommend rolling back the system-message tweak for the clinical-summary family while we test on the fixed preprocess pipeline.
[05:17] Dr. Miguel Santos: OK sounds reasonable. Any other blockers?
[05:21] Aisha Khan: one more - the scoring aggregator weights entity F1 at 0.4 and ROUGE-L at 0.6; given the clinical use case maybe give more weight to key-entity recall? We want false negatives on diagnoses to be minimized.
[05:36] Priya Patel: we can do that; we suggested testing two weightings in parallel and doing a human sample to pick the better tradeoff.
[05:44] Leo Park: what's the plan for the regression alerting? We want email + slack for >5% drop on any family.
[05:51] Jordan Lee: Redwood console can send both. We'll set a policy: alert if drop >3% for clinical-summary or >5% for other families. We can make that configurable.
[06:03] Aisha Khan: ok great. Could Priya also add the failed cases CSV to the ticket so we can triage by type?
[06:09] Priya Patel: yes I'll attach the failed_cases_20260305.csv to the shared drive.
[06:14] [00:06:14] Jordan Lee: next on list - dedicated vs hosted: given the latency hasn't changed much, do you still want to consider Dedicated for the pilot?
[06:22] Dr. Miguel Santos: maybe; cost is a concern but if we have strict throughput/latency needs for live triage we might want the predictability. Decide after we re-run the regression?
[06:30] Jordan Lee: yup we'll hold that decision. We'll also provide an estimated cost delta for Dedicated vs hosted for your current throughput.
[06:35] [00:06:35] Priya Patel: quick note on metrics: we'll produce a new sheet showing per-prompt family pass rates, delta from baseline, and failure buckets (tokenization, hallucination, format). That should help prioritize fixes.
[06:47] [00:06:47] Aisha Khan: one question on security - we need to ensure audit logs capture the inference inputs for compliance, but we also need PII redaction. Is that supported?
[06:55] Jordan Lee: yes Redwood Private and Dedicated both support configurable audit logs with KMS encryption; we also support deterministic PII redaction pre-store. We'll share the SOC2+security docs after this call.
[07:07] Dr. Miguel Santos: thanks.
[07:10] Jordan Lee: cool. Recap and actions: Jordan to share prompt variants and spreadsheet; Priya run regression with new thresholds and upload failed cases CSV; Aisha patch tokenization and upload sample data; all by dates in the action items. Also decision on Dedicated after regression re-run.
[07:28] Leo Park: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:31] [00:07:31] Jordan Lee: thanks; meeting adjourned.

Notes about transcript quality: Automated transcription had a few mislabels and occasional punctuation issues; speakers are manually verified. Shared artifacts: https://shared.redwood.app/poc/bluecrest/quality-eval.xlsx (prompt variants & eval sheet), s3://bluecrest-poc/samples/ (sample uploads), security-docs: https://redwood.app/security/soc2.pdf
